content: STEP 1 (design decision). Goal: pick a curvature mechanism that keeps the measured first-order gain and fixes the measured third-level collapse, without repeating the three rejected shapes (holonomy two-leg transport, GEOCAP popularity area-law radii, OCCURV-FIELD uniform-strength curvature field). Read: the round brief's measured chain (holonomy -> level2_distinct_prefixes=1, l3_collision=1.0; GEOCAP -> hard_er 3.885, hit 0.1222, l2_prefixes 4236, l3_collision 0.549; OCCURV-FIELD -> hard_er 2.488, hit 0.2629, l2_prefixes 784, l3_collision 0.943, all rejected by the 35% gate). Inference: every prior arm applied ONE curvature strength/sign at every level and attracted behaviour into the quantizer, so level 3 (which must DISAMBIGUATE, not group) paid the whole price and squeezed codeword usage. Design chosen: a per-level SIGNED curvature ladder, kappa_l = s_curv[l]*kappa_0*2^-(l-1) with s_curv=[-1,-1,+1] (shallow Poincare, deep sphere), and the SAME sign table orients a per-pair behaviour occupancy term placed INSIDE the argmin assignment score: score = d_{M(kappa_l)}(exp(r_l), exp(c_l[k])) + sigma_l*gamma_l*sum_j b_ij*1[khat_prev= k]. Shallow: attraction (shared prefix), deepest: repulsion (spread), so the deep level is explicitly de-collided. Behaviour signal: directed train-split transition log-odds b_ij with the threshold at independence (0) and clip at log T, both data-derived, no tuned constant; gamma_l = first-pass median top-1 curved distance (frozen). Open: nothing left to decide; the full block is in the next record.

STEP 2 (final answer, complete block). IDEA: signcurv-ladder-rq-2026
TITLE: Signed per-level curvature ladder with behaviour-oriented pair occupancy: shallow Poincare attraction, deepest-level spherical repulsion, both inside the RQ argmin
MOTIVATION: In a 3-level RQ-VAE SID, the shallow levels must GROUP behaviour-adjacent items (a shared prefix is what lets the generator name the next item's neighbourhood) while the deepest level must SEPARATE behaviour-confusable items (otherwise the last token cannot disambiguate which successor actually comes next). All three previously run curvature arms used one sign and one strength at every level, which bought level-1 separation (hard_er 2.488-3.885 vs 16.390 baseline, hit 0.0794->0.1222-0.2629) and then destroyed level-3 usage (l3_collision 0.549 / 0.943 / 1.0), so the SID was rejected by the 35% gate and Stage3 could not benefit.
NOVELTY: Not holonomy transport, not popularity-derived capacity radii, not a per-occupant curvature field of uniform strength. Here the CURVATURE SIGN ITSELF is a per-level ladder (negative shallow -> positive deepest, magnitude halving per level) and the SAME sign table orients a per-pair behaviour-occupancy term that lives inside the assignment score, so behaviour ATTracts on shallow levels and REPELS on the deepest level; the behaviour weight is a train-split transition log-odds thresholded at independence, not a tuned constant.
CHANGE: The RQ assignment at level l becomes argmin_k of a curved geodesic distance on M(kappa_l) (Poincare ball if kappa_l<0, sphere if kappa_l>0) plus sigma_l*gamma_l times the transition-log-odds mass of behaviour neighbours already occupying code k, with exp/log maps used identically for residual and codeword positions.
SPECIFICATION: PARAMS: L=3; K=codebook size (baseline 256); d=latent width; tangent codebooks c_l in R^{K x d}; ladder s_curv=[-1,-1,+1]; sigma=s_curv; R_bar=detach(rms over the first training batch of ||z||); kappa_0=1/R_bar^2 (frozen); kappa_l=s_curv[l]*kappa_0*2^-(l-1). BEHAVIOUR (built once, train split only): n_ij=count of consecutive (i->j); n_i=out mass; T=sum n_ij; b_ij=clip(log(n_ij*T/(n_i*n_j)),0,log T)/log T. FORWARD: z=Enc(x); r_1=z; for l=1..L: u_l=exp_{k_l}(r_l); p_lk=exp_{k_l}(c_l[k]); dist_lk=d_{k_l}(u_l,p_lk); nb_lk=scatter_sum_{j in N(i) and in batch} b_ij*1[khat_{l,j}^{prev}=k]; score_lk=dist_lk+sigma_l*gamma_l*nb_lk; k_l=argmin_k score_lk; rhat_l=r_l+sg(c_l[k_l]-r_l); r_{l+1}=r_l-c_l[k_l]; xhat=Dec(sum_l c_l[k_l]); SID(i)=(k_1,k_2,k_3). gamma_l=frozen median of min_k dist_lk over the first forward batch. Loss = baseline RQ-VAE reconstruction + commitment on c_l[k_l]; the behaviour term exists only inside the argmin (no extra loss weight to tune). Occupancy buffer khat^{prev} from the previous epoch, no_grad, refreshed once per epoch.
COST: Same number of forward/backward passes (3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps), same batch sizes; extra per step is 2 exp/log maps and L*K geodesic-distance evaluations over d-dim vectors (closed form tanh/atanh or tan/arccos, no iteration) plus a sparse scatter over in-batch behaviour pairs (~10-30 neighbours per anchor), i.e. about +5 to +10 percent wall clock per step and +0.02 GB memory (occupancy buffer 24556 x 3 x int16 = 0.15 MB, plus the sparse b_ij table on train items). No extra epoch, no ablation arm, no sweep, no second seed.
HYPOTHESIS: If the level-3 collapse was caused by one-sign curvature attracting behaviour-adjacent items into the same deep code,

then the sign-flipped deep level plus the per-pair repulsion must move l3_collision from the observed 0.55-1.0 down to <=0.35 while keeping valid_l1_hard_er <=4 and positive_hit_rate >=0.12 and level2_distinct_prefixes in the thousands, and Stage3 test_recall@10 must exceed 0.065 (baseline 0.0555, best 0.0638). It is falsified if l3_collision stays above 0.5, or if hard_er returns to the 16.4 baseline magnitude, or if refinement bits drop below the 2.32 bits of OCCURV-FIELD.
RISKS: ["Repulsion restricted to behaviour neighbours may not de-collide the many items with no in-batch neighbour, leaving l3_collision above the 35% gate.", "The frozen first-batch median gamma_l can be mis-scaled if the first batch is atypical, making the behaviour term either inert or dominant at level 3.", "The sphere level (kappa_3>0) bounds distances, so arccos gradients can saturate near-antipodal codewords and freeze their learning.", "The previous-epoch occupancy buffer lags, so the term can push items into a code that the next epoch then vacates, producing oscillation of l3 usage.", "Even with a clean SID, Stage3 may not convert the gain if the generator's prefix likelihood does not exploit the extra level-3 distinction."]
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-transition log-odds (behaviour-conditioned pair weight) over consecutive items of TRAIN sequences, restricted at use time to pairs whose both endpoints are in the current batch.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: One pass over TRAIN sequences only: n_ij = number of consecutive (i->j) transitions, n_i = sum_j n_ij, T = sum_ij n_ij; b_ij = clip(log(n_ij*T/(n_i*n_j)), 0, log T)/log T, so 0 means 'no more than chance' (threshold at independence) and 1 means 'maximally over-represented'. Stored as a sparse train-item x train-item table, plus the per-epoch hard SID buffer khat^{prev}_{l,i} produced by forward passes over TRAIN items only.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition counts, the b_ij table and the occupancy buffer are built exclusively from TRAIN sequences and TRAIN items; validation interactions are used only after an epoch to log diagnostics, never to build codes, curvatures, gamma_l, R_bar or b_ij; no test interaction of any kind enters SID construction. New (cold) items get zero rows in b_ij and are quantized by the curved distance alone, so the mechanism cannot smuggle validation co-occurrence into a prefix.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Closed-form exponential and logarithmic maps and geodesic distance of a signed-curvature manifold: Poincare ball of radius 1/sqrt(|kappa_l|) when kappa_l<0 (exp_k(x)=tanh(sqrt(|k|)||x||)/(sqrt(|k|)||x||) x, d_k=(1/sqrt|k|) arcosh(1+2|k||u-v|^2/((1-|k||u|^2)(1-|k||v|^2)))); sphere of radius 1/sqrt(kappa_l) when kappa_l>0 (exp_k(x)=tan(sqrt(k)||x||)/(sqrt(k)||x||) x, d_k=(1/sqrt(k)) arccos(clamp(k<u,v>))); identity/L2 when kappa_l=0. Base curvature kappa_0=1/R_bar^2 with R_bar the measured RMS latent norm, ladder kappa_l=s_curv[l]*kappa_0*2^-(l-1), s_curv=[-1,-1,+1].
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the Stage-2 RQ-VAE training loop, jointly in (a) the residual entry exp_{kappa_l}(r_l), (b) the codeword position exp_{kappa_l}(c_l[k]) and the reconstruction log_{kappa_l}, and (c) the geodesic distance that forms the assignment score, at every level l=1..3 with the level-dependent sign and magnitude.
COUPLING PATH: A single score -- the per-level argmin score -- is the meeting point: the curved geodesic distance defines the geometry of the term and the behaviour occupancy mass is added to the same sc

alar before the argmin, and both are oriented by the same per-level sign table sigma_l=s_curv[l]. Setting b_ij=0 leaves a pure signed-ladder curved RQ (the geometry still chooses every code); setting kappa_l=0 makes the distance and the maps Euclidean while the sigma ladder and the behaviour mass keep acting, so the same code path still assigns differently. Removing either therefore changes the actual discrete code selected at every level, not a side loss.
COUPLING EQUATION: score_{l,i,k} = d_{M(kappa_l)}( exp_{kappa_l}(r_{l,i}), exp_{kappa_l}(c_l[k]) ) + sigma_l * gamma_l * sum_{j in N(i)} b_ij * 1[khat_{l,j}^{prev} = k], with sigma_l = s_curv[l] and k_{l,i} = argmin_k score_{l,i,k}.
OBSERVABLES: l3_collision (must fall below 0.35), level2_distinct_prefixes (must stay in the thousands), valid_l1_hard_er (<=4), positive_hit_rate (>=0.12), refinement bits (>=2.3), per-level usage entropy and top-1 codeword share per level, prefix next-item predictability (conditional entropy of the true successor given each prefix length), and Stage3 test_recall@10 as the only judgement (target >0.065).
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: b_ij:=0 for all pairs, giving a pure signed-curvature-ladder RQ (exp/log residual entry, geodesic assignment, sphere deep level) with the behaviour mass absent; the switch exists and is unit-checked, but no arm is trained in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: kappa_l:=0 for all l, so exp/log become identity, distances become Euclidean L2 and codewords are plain points, while sigma_l and the behaviour occupancy mass stay active; this isolates what the curvature contributes to the same coupled score. Switch exists and is unit-checked, no arm trained.
ABLATION BOTH ON: the full mechanism exactly as specified (signed ladder with kappa_0=1/R_bar^2 and s_curv=[-1,-1,+1], train-split b_ij, gamma_l frozen from the first batch) -- this is the ONE candidate that is trained, for 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards and then the frozen Stage3 protocol.
SPEC EQUATIONS: kappa_0 = 1/R_bar^2, R_bar = detach(rms_batch(||z||)) computed once and checkpointed; kappa_l = s_curv[l]*kappa_0*2^-(l-1), s_curv=[-1,-1,+1]; b_ij = clip(log(n_ij T/(n_i n_j)),0,log T)/log T; gamma_l = detach(median over the first batch of min_k d_{M(kappa_l)}(exp(r_{l,i}),exp(c_l[k]))); u_l = exp_{kappa_l}(r_l); p_lk = exp_{kappa_l}(c_l[k]); score_lk = d_{M(kappa_l)}(u_l,p_lk) + sigma_l gamma_l sum_{j in N(i) inter batch} b_ij 1[khat_{l,j}^{prev}=k]; k_l = argmin_k score_lk; rhat_l = r_l + sg(c_l[k_l]-r_l); r_{l+1} = r_l - c_l[k_l]; L = ||x - Dec(sum_l c_l[k_l])||^2 + beta sum_l ||r_l - sg(c_l[k_l])||^2 (baseline beta), no additional weight on the behaviour term because it acts only through the argmin.
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: encoder latent z (width d) for each train item; the L tangent codebooks c_l (K x d); the sparse train-split b_ij table; the previous-epoch SID buffer khat^{prev}. Outputs: one SID per item (k_1,k_2,k_3) and its prefix hierarchy, the per-level quantized tangent vectors c_l[k_l] fed to the decoder, updated codebooks, the refreshed SID buffer at the end of each epoch, and the stored constants R_bar, kappa_l and gamma_l kept in the checkpoint for exact reproduction.
SAFEGUARDS: clamp the ball radius ||u|| <= (1-1e-3)/sqrt(|kappa|) before arcosh; use the series 2 artanh(x)/x -> 2 for small sqrt(|kappa|)||x|| and 2 arctan(x)/x -> 2 for small sqrt(kappa)||x|| to avoid 0/0; clamp arccos argument to [-(1-1e-6), 1-1e-6]; clamp sqrt(kappa)||r|| < pi/(2 sqrt(kappa))

- 1e-3 before tan so sphere points stay inside the chart; guard the Poincare denominator (1-|kappa||u|^2) with 1e-8; freeze gamma_l and R_bar after the first forward pass and mask them from the optimizer; build the occupancy buffer and the b_ij table under no_grad; skip the behaviour term for anchors with no in-batch neighbour and for cold items; fall back to Euclidean assignment (kappa_l=0) if R_bar is zero or non-finite; keep the straight-through path and the commitment loss so the encoder cannot collapse to a constant as it did in the holonomy run; log per-level usage entropy every epoch so a level-3 collapse is visible without gating on it.
END IDEA
